a1_team_name: Tiri (external name to be confirmed: arbitr Model Factory)
a1_one_line: We build and govern translation, quality and customer-trained models that run inside arbitr.
a1_produce: Custom language models, quality and risk models, LLM post-editors, and models trained on one customer's own content.
a1_track_record: Twelve models in production since 2023, across legal, life sciences and product content.
a1_coverage: EN into DE, FR, ES, IT, NL and JA in production; EN into PT and KO in beta. Legal, life sciences, marketing and UI content.
a1_expertise: Nine people: three ML engineers, two research scientists, three computational linguists and one evaluation lead.
a1_differentiator: Every model is evaluated on held-out customer-style content and released only through arbitr's assurance levels, so a human signs off before anything is published.
a3_base_models: In-house transformer MT engines (proprietary); open-weight LLM post-editors under Apache 2.0 licences.
a3_training: Full fine-tune for language models; adapters for customer-trained builds; no training from scratch.
a3_data_sources: Licensed corpora (about 60%), public-domain legal and regulatory text (about 30%), synthetic back-translation (about 10%). No customer data in shared models.
a3_feedback: Approved human edits and Cortex terminology feed a quarterly retraining cycle; edits are used only with the customer's consent.
a3_build_time: Six to eight weeks from an approved request to a production model.
a3_min_data: Around fifty thousand approved segments plus a glossary gives a measurable gain for a customer-trained build.
a3_compute: Training on reserved GPU capacity in AWS eu-central-1; each model build costs roughly EUR 1,800 in compute.
a4_auto_metrics: COMET-22 and chrF for translation models; precision, recall and calibration for quality and risk models.
a4_human_eval: MQM annotation by two qualified linguists per language, with inter-rater agreement reported for every release.
a4_test_sets: Held out by document, frozen before training, and checked for overlap with training data before each release.
a4_comparators: DeepL Pro and Google Translate, re-run every quarter on the same test sets.
a4_release_gate: A new model must beat the previous release on COMET-22 and show no increase in critical MQM errors.
a4_reeval: Every production model is re-tested each quarter and whenever its training data changes.
a5_customer_data: Customer content is never used to train shared models. Customer-trained builds use only that customer's content, with written opt-in.
a5_isolation: Each customer's content, fine-tuned weights and logs sit in separate storage and are never pooled with other customers.
a5_retention: Training data is kept for the life of the model; customers can ask for their data and model to be deleted at any time.
a5_residency: Content is stored and processed in the EU (Frankfurt). UK and US regions are available on request.
a5_pii: Named-entity detection masks personal data before any content is used for training; masked spans are reviewed by a linguist.
a5_provenance: Licence records are kept for every training corpus and reviewed by Legal before each release.
a5_subprocessors: AWS (hosting and storage). No third-party MT or LLM providers process customer content.
a6_hosting: Runs on AWS in eu-central-1, with a single-tenant deployment option for enterprise customers.
a6_certs: SOC 2 Type II report available; ISO 27001 certification in progress.
a6_encryption: AES-256 at rest and TLS 1.2+ in transit; keys managed in AWS KMS with yearly rotation.
a6_access: Model weights and training data are accessible only to the model team, with every access logged.
a6_ownership: Customers own the weights of any model trained on their content, and can export them or have them deleted at contract end.
a6_sec_testing: Annual external penetration test; the latest report is dated August 2026.
a7_eu_ai_act: Our translation models are not high-risk under the EU AI Act; we meet the transparency obligations by labelling machine-translated output.
a7_gdpr: Legitimate interest for licensed and public data; a DPA is available for every customer.
a7_bias: We test gender, formality and register consistency for every release and publish the results in the model card.
a7_oversight: Models run under arbitr assurance levels: at level 2 and above, a qualified reviewer approves every segment before publishing.
a7_incidents: Model failures are logged, triaged within one business day and disclosed to affected customers with a fix plan.
a7_docs: Customers receive a model card and an evaluation report at go-live, and a quality dashboard after launch.
a8_availability: Hosted models carry a 99.9% monthly uptime SLA.
a8_monitoring: Weekly automatic scoring of live output flags quality drift for human review.
a8_versioning: Versions follow major.minor numbering, are announced two weeks before release, and can be rolled back within a day.
a8_deprecation: At least ninety days' notice before a model version is retired.
a8_support: Email and in-app support during EU business hours, with a one-business-day response target.
a9_request_process: Reps request a model in the Model Factory; the model team replies within two working days.
